topics.topic: India emerges as Global Leader in issuing Compliance Certificates under Nagoya Protocol
topics.why_in_news: India emerged as global leader in issuing Internationally Recognized Certificates of Compliance (IRCCs) under Nagoya Protocol, reflecting strong implementation of Access and Benefit Sharing framework.
prelims_quick_notes: Nagoya Protocol operates under Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
Focuses on Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) of genetic resources.
IRCCs ensure compliance with Prior Informed Consent and Mutually Agreed Terms.
India issued more than 56% of global IRCCs.
Biological Diversity Act, 2002 governs ABS implementation in India.
National Biodiversity Authority implements biodiversity governance framework.
ABS aims at fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources.
Traditional knowledge protection linked with biodiversity governance.
key_findings_and_indicators: Only 34 of 142 registered countries issued IRCCs.
India significantly outperformed other participating countries.
Three-tier biodiversity governance structure operational in India.
important_facts: Nagoya Protocol entered into force in 2014.
ABS Clearing-House ensures transparency and monitoring.
Prior Informed Consent mandatory before resource access.
Mutually Agreed Terms govern benefit-sharing arrangements.
National Biodiversity Authority functions under Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
exam_relevance: Important for Environment, Biodiversity and International Environmental Governance.
Useful for CBD, SDGs and traditional knowledge protection topics.
Can be linked with bio-economy, conservation and climate governance.
prelims_traps: Nagoya Protocol functions under CBD framework.
IRCCs relate to Access and Benefit Sharing compliance.
Biological Diversity Act, 2002 governs biodiversity regulation in India.
Prior Informed Consent and Mutually Agreed Terms are core ABS concepts.
